experimental_method: Chemical: Winkler titration of water saturated with air in a thermostatted counter-current saturator (triplicate); physical: gasometric saturation with pure O2 as in Part I.
uncertainties_stated: Chemical accuracy about 0.01 ml O2/l (replicate SD 0.008 ml/l at 20 C); temperature control 0.022 C (chemical) and 0.017 C (physical); chlorinity accuracy better than 0.01 permil; physical replicate SDs 0.010, 0.007, 0.006 ml/l at 13.60, 25.72, 28.31 C.
quality_remarks: Winkler results include a 0.011 ml/l reagent-oxygen correction. Results agree with Carpenter (1966) to about 0.006 ml/l on average; Green and Carritt tables deviate up to 1-1.7 percent. Source says Table 1 and Table 3 are on a ml/l basis from air (20.94 % O2, 100 % RH); the physical values were converted by the authors. Text layer is OCR-like with quote marks for decimal points.

not_extracted_tables.reason: smoothed curve oxygen solubility values at integral T and chlorinity (fitted/derived), pdf page 6 / journal p. 316

extraction_notes: Both tables transcribed from the page images; a script cross-check against the text layer found the only disagreement was one text-layer damage (10.021 read as 0.021 at 0.74 C, S=0.000). Because the text layer is unusable for decimals, a blind second pass is recommended. No sanity violations found: solubility decreases with T and with salinity within each block.
needs_pass2_reason: text layer unreliable (OCR with quote characters as decimals); all cells read from image
pass2_diff: token diff: Table 3 identical; Table 1 every number of pass 2 found in pass 1, extras are carried-forward temperatures
